standard_attempts_log.asr_text: Sometimes a person opens their eyes just before the alarm rings. It can feel like a small mystery. Did the body know the time? The human body has a built-in clock. Light helps this clock match the 24-hour day. Regular sleep and wake times can also help. In a laboratory study, weak light and regular routines usually matched a 24-hour day. They did not usually match shorter or longer days.

full_story_part1.canonical_text:
Sometimes, a person opens their eyes just before the alarm rings.

It can feel like a small mystery. Did the body know the time?

The human body has a built-in clock. Light helps this clock match the twenty-four-hour day. Regular sleep and wake times can also help. In a laboratory study, weak light and regular routines usually matched a twenty-four-hour day. They did not usually match shorter or longer days.

full_story_part2.text: Researchers also study a related ability called self-awakening: waking near a planned time without an outside signal. A review found many studies involving hundreds of people. But the studies used different rules. In many of them, waking within 30 minutes of the planned time counted as success. So, the body may prepare for an expected waking time. But research does not yet show that the body can predict the exact moment an alarm will ring.

full_story_part2.canonical_text:
Researchers also study a related ability called self-awakening: waking near a planned time without an outside signal.

A review found many studies involving hundreds of people. But the studies used different rules. In many of them, waking within 30 minutes of the planned time counted as success.

So, the body may prepare for an expected waking time. But research does not yet show that the body can predict the exact moment an alarm will ring.

point_one.text: The preparation does not seem to be one sudden event. In one study, a hormone called ACTH rose about one hour before waking when people expected sleep to end. In another, activity in the front-right part of the brain changed about 30 minutes before successful self-awakening. In a short nap study, heart rate began to rise about 3 minutes before waking. Together, these findings suggest a slow build-up toward waking. A person may become physically ready before becoming fully conscious.

point_two.text: The body's preparation is only part of the story. Near the end of a normal night, deep sleep becomes less common, while lighter sleep and dream sleep become more common. Waking from deep sleep is linked with stronger grogginess than waking from lighter sleep. This may help explain why one morning feels easy, while another feels much harder.
